issues.description: Class 'Animal' constructor signature and attributes differ between the problem statement UML and the solution code. The problem statement (UML) declares Animal with two attributes (name: String and age: int) and a constructor '+ Animal(String, int)'. The solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) defines only a single 'name' attribute and a constructor 'Animal(String)'. This discrepancy leaves students uncertain whether they must implement an 'age' field and a two-parameter constructor (String, int) as shown in the UML or a single-parameter constructor as in the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and code consistent. Either: (A) Update problem_statement.md (UML) to show Animal with only the 'name' attribute and constructor 'Animal(String)', or (B) Update the template and solution to include the 'age' attribute and change the constructor to 'Animal(String, int)' (add getter/setter for age and update all subclass constructors and any instantiation sites such as Main and tests to pass an age). Apply the chosen design consistently across the UML, template, solution, and tests so students know which constructor and attributes to implement.
